chunks: 2036 - Al-Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā narrated from his grandfather Al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “The people say that forgiveness descends upon the one who fasted the month of Ramaḍān on Laylat al-Qadr.” So he said: “O Ḥasan, the wage-earner is only given his wage when he finishes his work, and that is the night of ʿĪd.”

I said: “May I be your ransom, then what should we do on that night?” He said: “When the sun sets, pray the three of Maghrib, raise your hands, and say: O Possessor of bounty, O Possessor of power, O Chooser of Muḥammad and his Helper, send blessings upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and forgive me every sin I committed and forgot, while it is with You in a clear book. Then fall in prostration and say one hundred times: I repent to Allah, while you are prostrating, and ask for your needs.”
ai.seo_question: What should be recited and done on the night of ʿĪd al-Fiṭr after Maghrib according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the completion-reward of the month of Ramaḍān is associated with the night of ʿĪd al-Fiṭr, likening the fasting person to a worker paid after finishing his task. It also instructs a specific post-Maghrib supplication and sajdah of repentance, emphasizing seeking forgiveness, salat upon Muḥammad and Āl Muḥammad, and asking Allah for one’s needs.
